subtitle: How Budshah Bent the Waters of Kashmir

panels.shot: epic bird's-eye of Wular Lake with a half-formed stone island emerging from the water
panels.action: Zain-ul-Abidin stands on a boat at dawn, arm outstretched toward a rising stone embankment in Wular Lake, engineers and laborers swarming over the half-born island.

dialogue.text: In the age of Budshah Zain-ul-Abidin, the waters of Kashmir were bent by human will—an island raised from Wular, bridges and embankments carved, so fields and cities could breathe.

i18n.hi: बडशाह ज़ैनुलआबिदीन के दौर में इंसानी इरादे से पानी झुके — वुलर से टापू उठा, पुल–बंध बने, ताकि खेत और शहर सांस ले सकें।

panels.shot: slow push-in across flooded fields toward a contemplative ruler
panels.action: Zain-ul-Abidin stands on a muddy riverbank near Sopore, looking over drowned fields and scattered huts as peasants wade through knee-deep water.

dialogue.text: Each year the Jhelum and the lakes rose, swallowing crops and paths. Under Budshah, Kashmir’s prosperity would depend on whether its waters could be tamed.

i18n.hi: हर साल झेलम और झीलें चढ़तीं, फसलें और राह निगल जातीं। बडशाह के राज में कश्मीर की खुशहाली इस बात पर टिकी थी कि पानी काबू में आए या नहीं।

panels.shot: medium low-angle on Zain-ul-Abidin among engineers and scribes
panels.action: Zain-ul-Abidin sits beneath a deodar tree, surrounded by builders, masons and scribes who spread rough maps and wooden measuring rods on the ground.

dialogue.speaker: zain_ul_abidin
dialogue.text: Fields must not drown while palaces stand dry. Show me how we break this pattern.

i18n.hi: खेत न डूबें जबकि महल सूखे रहें। दिखाओ, ये चक्र कैसे तोड़ते हैं।

panels.shot: sweeping wide shot of Wular Lake’s expanse dotted with boats
panels.action: A panoramic view of Wular Lake stretches under cloudy skies, wooden boats gliding over rippled water, distant hills and clustered villages hugging the shore.

dialogue.text: Srivara’s Jaina-Rajatarangini tells of Wular, vast and restless. In its heart Budshah planned an island—Zaynalank—fortified, ordered, a symbol of rule over water.

i18n.hi: श्रीवरा की जैन राजतरंगिणी वुलर का ज़िक्र करती है — विशाल, बेक़रार। इसी के दिल में बडशाह ने टापू सोचा — ज़ैनलंक — किले जैसा, सधा हुआ, पानी पर राज का निशान।

panels.shot: dynamic overhead shot of men dumping stones from boats
panels.action: Dozens of laborers on small boats and rafts haul baskets of stones and earth, tipping them into the shallow center of Wular as overseers point and shout directions.

dialogue.text: Stone by stone, basket by basket, they began to feed the lake. The island was not found; it was constructed, its bones sunk deep where the waters were least fierce.

i18n.hi: पत्थर–पत्थर, टोकरी–टोकरी, उन्होंने झील को भरना शुरू किया। टापू मिला नहीं, बनाया गया; इसकी हड्डियाँ वहीं गड़ीं जहाँ पानी कम उग्र था।

panels.shot: low-angle close-up of a stone embankment rising above water
panels.action: A solid stone embankment rises from the water, its edges wet and glistening, waves slapping harmlessly against the newly laid masonry.

dialogue.text: Srivara describes a stone embankment girding Zaynalank. Its purpose was practical and symbolic: to hold back the lake and to advertise the Sultan’s control over its moods.

i18n.hi: श्रीवरा ज़ैनलंक को घेरे पत्थर की क़िलेबंदी का वर्णन करता है। मक़सद काम का भी था और नाम का भी — झील को रोकना और सुल्तान की पकड़ दिखाना।

panels.shot: wide architectural shot of the island with structures forming
panels.action: On the rising island, wooden scaffolds surround an emerging palace and mosque; terraced garden plots are marked out, saplings ready for planting.

dialogue.text: On Zaynalank rose a palace, a mosque, and gardens. A seat of authority placed upon water, close enough to watch the lake, firm enough to withstand its force.

i18n.hi: ज़ैनलंक पर महल, मस्जिद और बाग़ उगे। पानी पर बिठाया तख़्त, झील पर नज़र रखने को क़रीब, उसकी मार झेलने को मज़बूत।

panels.shot: interior medium shot of Budshah walking through his island garden
panels.action: Zain-ul-Abidin strolls along a newly laid path on the island, shaded by young trees, water shimmering beyond the embankment stones.

dialogue.text: From Zaynalank Budshah could look out over Wular, the lake now held in a stone embrace. But the real work lay on the flooded shores of Sopore and Safapur.

i18n.hi: ज़ैनलंक से बडशाह वुलर पर नज़र डाल सकता था, झील अब पत्थरों की बाँहों में थी। पर असली काम सोपोर और सफ़ापुर के डूबे किनारों पर था।

panels.shot: expansive wide shot of Sopore-Safapur plain with survey markers
panels.action: Surveyors and laborers plant wooden stakes across a broad marshy plain between Sopore and Safapur, while villagers watch anxiously from raised patches of land.

dialogue.text: Mohibbul Hasan and Lawrence record an embankment between Sopore and Safapur. It was designed to check floods and win new farmland from the waterlogged margins.

i18n.hi: मोहिब्बुल हसन और लॉरेन्स सोपोर–सफ़ापुर के बीच बंध का ज़िक्र करते हैं। इसका नक़्शा ऐसा था कि बाढ़ रुके और गीली ज़मीन से नए खेत जीत लिए जाएं।

panels.shot: side-on medium shot of peasants piling earth, overseers directing
panels.action: Peasants with baskets and spades pile earth and stones into a long rising dyke, overseers marking its curve while the Jhelum flows sullenly beside.

dialogue.text: The embankment was labor-intensive, built by hands used to sowing, now trained to engineer. Its curve had to channel overflow, not simply block it, or disaster would return.

i18n.hi: ये बंध मेहनत माँगता था — बोआई की आदतवाले हाथ अब इंजीनियर बने। इसकी मोड़ ऐसी रखनी थी कि उफान को दिशा मिले, बस रोकें नहीं, वरना फिर कहर लौट आता।

panels.shot: celebratory wide shot of dry fields where water once stood
panels.action: Formerly marshy land now lies dry; furrows are plowed, grain is sown, and simple mud houses rise along a new raised road.

dialogue.text: As the works settled, land that had seen only reeds began to see grain. Traces in topography today still echo these embankments that turned flooded margins into cultivable fields.

i18n.hi: जैसे–जैसे काम बैठा, जहाँ सिर्फ़ सरकंडे उगते थे, वहाँ अनाज दिखने लगा। आज की ज़मीन की शक्ल में भी उन बंधों की गूँज है, जिन्होंने डूबे किनारों को खेत बनाया।

panels.shot: wide shot of Dal Lake with a straight causeway cutting across
panels.action: Dal Lake gleams under clear skies as a sturdy earthen causeway cuts a straight line across shallow water, carts and pedestrians moving between banks.

dialogue.text: Srivara also notes causeways over Dal and near Andarkot. These were not mere conveniences; they pulled distant shores into the orbit of Srinagar’s markets and officials.

i18n.hi: श्रीवरा दल और अंदरकोट के पास पतरीले रास्तों का भी ज़िक्र करता है। ये सिर्फ़ सहूलत नहीं थे; इन्होंने दूर किनारों को श्रीनगर के बाज़ारों और अफ़सरों की पहुँच में खींच लिया।

panels.shot: medium shot of Budshah watching traffic cross the Dal causeway
panels.action: Zain-ul-Abidin stands on the Dal causeway, watching traders with pack animals and farmers with produce walking confidently over water that once demanded boats.

dialogue.text: With firm paths across water, movement became predictable. Taxes could be collected, messages carried, grain moved before rot and flood, stitching lake communities to the capital.

i18n.hi: पानी पर पक्की राहों से आना–जाना ठिकाने पर हुआ। लगान वसूला जा सका, संदेश पहुँचे, अनाज सड़ने और बाढ़ से पहले पहुँचा, झील किनारे के लोग राजधानी से जुड़ गए।

panels.shot: establishing shot of Srinagar with the Jhelum winding through
panels.action: A sweeping view of Srinagar shows houses and gardens lining the twisting Jhelum, wooden bridges in the distance, boats gliding in the river’s bends.

dialogue.text: In Srinagar the Jhelum still curved through the city, a lifeline and a barrier. A single reliable bridge could change how the capital breathed and grew.

i18n.hi: श्रीनगर में झेलम अब भी शहर को मोड़ कर बहती थी — जान भी, रुकावट भी। एक भरोसेमंद पुल राजधानी की साँस और बढ़त बदल सकता था।

panels.shot: heroic low-angle of Zain-ul-Abidin overseeing bridge construction
panels.action: Zain-ul-Abidin stands on a temporary wooden platform over the Jhelum as carpenters and laborers raise stout piers and lay heavy beams for a permanent bridge.

dialogue.text: Srivara credits Budshah with Zaina Kadal, the bridge that still bears his name. It bound banks together and drew the city tighter around the river’s spine.

i18n.hi: श्रीवरा बडशाह को ज़ैनाकदाल का श्रेय देता है — पुल जो आज भी उसका नाम लिए है। इसने दोनों किनारे बाँधे और शहर को नदी की रीढ़ पर कस कर बैठा दिया।

panels.shot: majestic wide shot of completed Zaina Kadal busy with traffic
panels.action: The completed Zaina Kadal spans the Jhelum, crowded with pedestrians, traders, and officials; boats pass quietly beneath its arches.

dialogue.text: Over Zaina Kadal passed merchants, clerks, and common folk. A bridge like this was a piece of administration in timber and stone, more enduring than many decrees.

i18n.hi: ज़ैनाकदाल से व्यापारी, मुंशी और आम लोग गुज़रे। ऐसा पुल लकड़ी–पत्थर में बना एक प्रशासनिक औज़ार था, कई फ़रमानों से ज़्यादा टिकाऊ।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a tall wooden palace at Naushahr
panels.action: Zain-ul-Abidin walks through a lofty wooden hall at Naushahr, pillars rising high, water channels cut neatly along the floor to feed inner fountains.

dialogue.text: Tarikh-i-Rashidi later praises Budshah’s Naushahr palace as soaring, with many rooms and piped water. The details may be embellished, but they reflect deliberate control of water in architecture.

i18n.hi: तारीख़–ए–रशीदी बाद में बडशाह के नौशहर महल को ऊँचा, कई कमरों वाला, नलों से बहते पानी वाला बताती है। बातें बढ़ा–चढ़ा कर हों, पर इमारत में पानी पर सोच–समझ कर काबू ज़रूर दिखता है।

panels.shot: close-up of water flowing through a carved stone spout
panels.action: Clear water pours through a carved stone spout into a basin inside the palace, artisans nearby adjusting channels and joints.

dialogue.text: Canals and pipes carried water into palaces, gardens, and workshops. Walter Lawrence saw their traces centuries later, remnants of a system that served both comfort and craft.

i18n.hi: नहरों और नलों से पानी महलों, बाग़ों और कारख़ानों तक आता था। सदियों बाद वॉल्टर लॉरेन्स ने उनके निशान देखे — एक ऐसे इंतज़ाम की बची हुई रगें जो आराम और हुनर दोनों को पानी देता था।

panels.shot: reflective medium close-up of Budshah gazing at river and city
panels.action: At dusk Zain-ul-Abidin stands on Zaina Kadal, looking down at the Jhelum and the lit houses lining its banks, the bridge steady under the flow of people.

dialogue.text: Srivara records palaces, mosques, islands, embankments, and bridges; Lawrence traces their imprint in land and water. Through them, Budshah’s rule still speaks—in fields saved, roads made, and rivers made safer to live beside.

i18n.hi: श्रीवरा महल, मस्जिदें, टापू, बंध और पुल गिनता है; लॉरेन्स ज़मीन और पानी पर उनके निशान पढ़ता है। इनके ज़रिए बडशाह की हुकूमत आज भी बोलती है — बचाए गए खेतों में, बनी राहों में, और उन नदियों में जो इंसान के साथ रहना सीख गईं।

subtitle_i18n.en: How Budshah Bent the Waters of Kashmir
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे बडशाह ने कश्मीर की धार मोड़ी
